components.description: Federal FMLA leave as restated in UW Regulation 5-1 G.4: twelve weeks of unpaid, job-protected family leave for a birth or placement, or medical leave for the employee's own serious health condition or to care for a spouse, child or parent. The Employee Handbook restates it for staff with more detail.
components.faculty_group_note: UW Reg 5-1 Section G, 'VACATION AND LEAVE FOR FACULTY, ACADEMIC PROFESSIONALS, AND UNIVERSITY OFFICERS': 'benefited employees'
components.eligible_parent_wording: 'birth or placement of a child with the employee' (Reg 5-1); Handbook: 'care for the employee's child after birth, or placement for adoption or foster care'; medical leave for the employee's own serious health condition or to care for a 'spouse'
components.service_requirement: 12 months of service (benefited employees; Reg 5-1); non-benefited employees 12 months and 1,250 hours
components.dual_employee_rule: combined 12 weeks for spouses both employed by the University, for care of a child after birth or placement (Handbook; 29 U.S.C. 2612(f)); not combined for the employee's own serious health condition
components.entitlement_note: Statutory entitlement (FMLA); Reg 5-1: 'are eligible for twelve (12) weeks of unpaid Family and Medical Leave'.
components.duration_note: Reg 5-1 states 'twelve (12) weeks' with no qualifier; the Handbook (staff) says 'up to 12 weeks'; the statute says 'a total of 12 workweeks' (R13: exact). Unpaid; the paid part depends only on the employee's own balances.
components.medical_certification_note: Health-care-provider certification required for Medical Leave (own serious health condition or care of a sick family member), not for Family Leave for a birth or placement.
components.time_window: Family Leave: the right 'usually expires twelve (12) months after the birth or placement of a child with the employee'
components.notice: at least thirty (30) days advance notice, unless not practical
components.return_obligation: reimburse University-paid health insurance premiums if the employee does not return after the leave, unless the failure is due to a serious health condition or circumstances beyond the employee's control
components.relief_note: A leave of absence; no relief stated (R9).

sequence.note: S1: the statutory leave runs alongside the institution's own leave for the birth (up to six weeks of sick leave for birth and first-year care). Reg 5-1 also says employees 'may not substitute paid Sick Leave for unpaid Family Leave'; the two readings are noted, the link only places the statute alongside.

notes: Governing document for faculty leave: UW Regulation 5-1 (12/14/2016 revisions), Section G 'Vacation and Leave for Faculty, Academic Professionals, and University Officers'. It is a faculty leave policy covering tenure-stream faculty, so missing is false (the rule for records with no governing document does not apply). It contains no parental leave, childbirth benefit, modified duties or parental tenure-clock provision; parents rely on FMLA, accrued sick leave (including up to six weeks for birth and first-year care) and general leaves.

UW Regulation 5-803 (tenure procedures, 2015) states no extension or stop of the probationary period; the only clock provision is Reg 5-1 D's request to modify the probationary period 'in exceptional cases' (c8, general_purpose).

The Employee Handbook (3/23/17) is adopted by UW Reg 4-174 as 'policies for Staff Employees'; its Section I is headed 'applicable to all employees' but its leave sections refer faculty to Reg 5-1. Where it restates a Reg 5-1 provision (FMLA, sick leave, donated sick leave, vacation) it is cited as supporting detail; provisions found only in the Handbook (medical leave for those not FMLA-eligible c9, leave without pay c10, leave with pay c11, LTD c12) are coded for staff and flagged ambiguous. Open rules question: if the Handbook's Section I applies to faculty, c9 (discretionary, 6 weeks after FMLA) and c12 would cover them.

Handbook I.D.20: 'The maximum length of leave of absence (LOA) for an employee is six months in a 12 month period' (staff; may be exceeded after review with HR); not recorded as a leave_limits entry because it caps no faculty components and is not a hard limit; noted in c9 and c10.

Calendar: the documents name a 'Fall semester' (Reg 5-1 G.2.c; Reg 5-803 3.e.viii) but state no term length; calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. No component is measured in terms.

Birth parent chain: FMLA 12 weeks (c1), with up to 6 weeks of own sick leave for birth and first-year care (c3) concurrent with it (S1); own accrued sick leave (c2) and donated leave (c4) pay part of it from balances only. [Staff only: Handbook medical leave up to 6 weeks (c9) consecutive_after FMLA.]

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 weeks (c1) (family leave for the birth, or medical leave to care for the spouse), with up to 6 weeks of own sick leave for birth and first-year care (c3) concurrent with it.

No employer-funded paid parental leave: the only paid time for a birth comes from the employee's own sick or vacation balances (payer own_balance) or from general-purpose emergency leave with pay (c6, discretionary, up to 4 weeks).

Documents cited but not saved: Presidential Directive 4-2004-2 (leave of absence with pay; flagged on c11); the University's Long Term Disability program plan (flagged on c12); UW Regulations 5-801, 5-808, 5-408, 5-35 (Appendix B), 6-41, 6-43, 6-702, 1-5, 1-34, 1-44, 2-39, 3-179, 4-2, 4-175, 7-490, 7-631, 8-256; Presidential Directives 4-2016-1, 4-2013-1 (pd-4-2013-1), 4-2010-2; the Academic Affairs document 'Expectations for Faculty Members' Presence on Campus'; the HR Background Review Policy. None of the unsaved regulations is named as a leave or parental provision except PD 4-2004-2 and the LTD plan.
The Handbook's link to UW Reg 5-1 points to the 2015 version, superseded by the 12/14/2016 revision used here.

Not components: Sabbatical Leave (professional development; cannot be taken for a birth), Academic Professional Development Leave (academic professionals; professional purpose), Bereavement Leave, Military Leave, Firefighting Leave, holidays, winter and emergency closures.
